findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited promises; other callers use calendar synchronously
findings.body: getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` in getCalendarCredentials is a Promise. getConnectedCalendars was updated to await it, but any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials (e.g. in the app or trpc code, not shown in this diff) that reads `.calendar` synchronously will call methods on a Promise and fail at runtime. The return type changed silently and should be audited or made explicit.

findings.title: async forEach callback: errors escape try/catch and the deletes are not awaited
findings.body: The forEach callback is now async, so rejections from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting become unhandled promise rejections. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch them. The function proceeds to send emails and return before the calendar and video deletions finish. In serverless environments the work may be cut off. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` inside the try. The same issue exists in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and trpc bookings.tsx requestReschedule.

findings.title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch the async forEach callback awaits getCalendar and then pushes into apiDeletes. Previously the getCalendar call was synchronous, so the callback body ran up to the first await. Now the push happens after the await, and the handler's `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` snapshots the array before those pushes. Recurring calendar deletions are never awaited, may silently fail, and may be dropped in serverless runtimes. Replace with a for...of loop or Promise.all over the credentials.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Each entry is `import(...)` evaluated when the object literal is built. Importing appStore therefore starts loading all ~29 apps immediately, with the same total cost as before, and a failing import becomes an unhandled rejection at load time. Real lazy loading needs thunks like `() => import(...)` or a lookup function. This PR changes the API to promises without delivering the intended benefit.
